key_insight: The paper introduces Turbo, a transformer-based reinforcement learning framework that lets microrobotic swarms navigate and avoid obstacles autonomously in unknown environments. Its key breakthrough is effective simulation-to-real transfer, bringing learned swarm behaviors from virtual training into physical robots.
problem_solved: Microrobotic swarms are hard to control in real-world, unknown environments because they must react to obstacles, uncertainty, and limited sensing while also transferring policies learned in simulation to real hardware.
method: Uses a transformer-based reinforcement learning policy to model swarm behavior and coordination.
Trains in simulation to learn navigation and obstacle avoidance strategies, then transfers the policy to physical microrobotic swarms.
Designed for autonomous decision-making in partially observed, unknown environments with robust sim-to-real transfer.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how transformers and reinforcement learning can be combined to control multi-agent robotic systems beyond simulation. It offers a practical path toward deploying learned policies in safety-critical, real-world swarm robotics.
visual_elements: Swarm navigation diagram showing robots moving through an unknown obstacle field.
Simulation-to-real pipeline graphic illustrating training in simulation and deployment on physical microrobots.
Transformer architecture icon or block diagram highlighting attention-based policy learning.
Before-and-after comparison of random vs. Turbo-guided swarm trajectories.
paper_title: Autonomous navigation of intelligent microrobotic swarms in unknown environments
paper_authors: Xuanyu An, Shengming Luo, Haoyu Zhang, Qijun Yang, Yuanbiao Ma
